The overview

Anchorage is the gateway to Alaska — a city ringed by mountains and water, minutes from glaciers, fjords and some of the best wildlife viewing on the continent.

Top things to do in Anchorage

  • See glaciers on a Kenai Fjords cruise
  • Ride the Alaska Railroad toward Denali
  • Spot moose, bears and bald eagles
  • Drive the scenic Seward Highway
  • Chase the northern lights (Sep–Mar)

Best time to visit

The sweet spot for Anchorage is generally Jun–Aug (long days) / Sep–Mar (auroras) — and the cheapest fares often land just outside peak season.

Is it safe?

Very safe; weather & wildlife are the main cautions. Watch your belongings in crowds and tourist areas, and check your government’s current advisory before you go. Visa for US passports: None for US citizens (Alaska is a US state).

A bit of history

Founded as a railroad construction camp in 1915, Anchorage grew with the military and the 1968 oil boom into Alaska’s largest city and the hub for exploring the 49th state.

Culture & language

Alaska blends frontier spirit with deep Alaska Native heritage; the outdoors is the culture here, with hiking, fishing and aurora-watching woven into daily life.

Language: English · English spoken: Native

Frequently asked questions

When is the best time to visit Anchorage?

The best time to fly to Anchorage is generally Jun–Aug (long days) / Sep–Mar (auroras). Shoulder-season trips often pair good weather with lower fares.

Is Anchorage safe for tourists?

Very safe; weather & wildlife are the main cautions. As anywhere, watch your belongings in crowds and check your government's current advisory before you go.

Do US citizens need a visa for Alaska, USA?

Visa for US passports: None for US citizens (Alaska is a US state). Always confirm the latest entry rules with official sources before booking.
